quotes.text: The Ship was cheer'd, the Harbour clear'd— / Merrily did we drop / Below the Kirk, below the Hill, / Below the Light-house top.
quotes.reference: 1798, Samuel Taylor Coleridge, The Rime of the Ancient Mariner:

quotes.text: When she sang in the kirk, folk have told me that they had a foretaste of the musick of the New Jerusalem, and when she came in by the village of Caulds old men stottered to their doors to look at her.
quotes.reference: 1902, John Buchan, The Outgoing of the Tide:

quotes.text: But long, long ago an enthusiastic reporter called it a "fairy palace," and the office building on the west side was once a church. Hence, in North British phraseology, to "gang tae the Kirk" meant to be had up on the carpet.
